source.title: Revisiting the Adam-SGD Gap in LLM Pre-Training: The Role of Large Effective Learning Rates
source.authors: Athanasios Glentis; Da-Wei Li; Chung-Yiu Yau; Ming-Yi Hong

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests optimizer-related held-out performance differences in LLM pre-training with a different setting and outcome measure from the claim’s listed optimizer comparisons.
record.gate_note: Main validation-loss comparisons and measured training-dynamics results bear on optimizer, batch-size, and model-size conditions. Cited prior studies and the theoretical bounds alone are not separate empirical rows. Hyperparameter ablations are included only where they report validation loss for the optimizer comparison.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam and momentum SGD on held-out language-model loss after learning-rate sweeps, extending V4 to decoder-only transformer pre-training. Adam performs better, qualifying the scope of SGD's advantage. It does not isolate generalization from optimization: SGD also has substantially worse training loss.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors attribute much of SGD's pre-training deficit to insufficient effective learning rates and show that targeted clipping permits much larger rates, closing most of the validation-loss gap while leaving a residual deficit to Adam.
record.recipe_differences: Language-model pre-training on C4 and FineWeb, comparing Adam, momentum SGD, and a clipping-modified large-learning-rate SGD; evaluation uses validation loss rather than image or language benchmark held-out accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: Model scale, token batch size, optimizer and clipping recipe, Adam β2, and AdamW weight decay are varied; main experiments use zero weight decay and report best learning-rate sweep results.

fits_no_version.finding: Targeted clipping enables high-learning-rate SGD to approach Adam, while retaining higher validation loss at every reported model scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-wise and output-token clipping can substantially reduce SGD's optimization and validation-loss deficit in large-batch language-model pre-training.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam's effective learning rates and update norms substantially exceed SGD's; weight-to-gradient ratios increase with batch size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-batch language-model training dynamics constrain the effective update size of ordinary SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-wise gradient spikes and token-frequency-dependent output-gradient disparities restrict stable high-learning-rate SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient irregularities help explain SGD's optimization deficit in language-model pre-training.

record.code_released: URL stated as “this link” in supplied text; no resolvable URL provided.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the main validation-loss table. Main optimizer comparisons report a single seed; four seeds are reported only for the 130M setting, and the 350M and 1B results lack repeated-seed estimates. The paper states its clipping method leaves a residual gap to Adam.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible additional claim-version outcome rows identified. Figure-only dynamics and token-frequency plots are not separately recorded as rows because the mapped versions concern held-out performance gaps, and those measurements do not directly measure the listed version outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under matched architectures and recipes.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.

Image benchmarks; word-level language-model benchmarks; held-out differences at matched training performance; a controlled comparison of limited versus broader tuning; recovery through decoupled weight decay or switching Adam to SGD.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes. Batch-dependent gradient statistics do not measure this outcome.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: Repeated-seed Adam-SGD comparisons for LLaMA 130M: Adam loss is 3.11 for all four seeds; SGD losses are 5.07, 6.13, 5.05 and 5.05. Add the three additional seed comparisons; the main result corresponds to seed 42.

record.verdict_notes: The record's supports label reverses V4's principal direction: worse SGD performance does not support an adaptive-optimizer disadvantage. Because V4 says often and already allows language-model exceptions, these results qualify its scope rather than refute it globally. The Adam-only tuning sweeps supply robustness context, not independent verdicts. Main-table uncertainty is unreported; Table 5 supplies repeated runs only for the 130M setting.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test generalization are not measured.
No width sweep of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison.

No image-classification or word-level language-model benchmarks; no broader tuning comparison against the listed optimizer studies. It tests SGD versus Adam on language-model pre-training, including a clipping-modified SGD variant.
No controlled large-batch versus small-batch comparison at fixed epoch budgets; reported batch sizes accompany different model scales and training token budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No removal of memorized training examples.

relationships.condition: LLaMA 130M, 350M and 1B pre-training on C4 with learning-rate sweeps, cosine schedules, zero weight decay and large token batches
relationships.reason: R1/R2, R4/R5 and R7/R8 show Adam losses of 3.11/2.78/2.51 versus SGD's 5.07/4.14/3.95. This extends the language-model qualification to the usual SGD advantage; Table 5 confirms the 130M ordering across four seeds.
relationships.display_finding: Adam had lower evaluation losses across the LLaMA models and also lower training loss, preventing isolation of a generalization effect.

reader_labels.condition: Momentum SGD versus Adam on C4 and FineWeb pre-training; SGD-LL versus Adam on the same settings
reader_labels.reason: SGD has higher validation loss than Adam, while clipping-modified SGD narrows most of the gap but remains slightly worse (R2, R3, R5, R6, R8, R9, R11, R12). This is partial support for the optimizer-gap pattern under the tested LLM pre-training recipes.
